clue.text: Boards scheme to get a royal connection

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
a king is a royal

explanation.surface: A plot is hatched to marry into the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'connection' simply join the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is a collective word for wooden boards laid as flooring or decking.

clue.text: Panted, jogging —— being a bookish person

indicators.note: jogging the letters shakes them up so they fall in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone out running, breathless, despite being a bookworm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' rearranges the letters of PANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone who shows off scholarly learning and fusses over details.

clue.text: A note sent off by representatives

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: off suggests the word sent has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some envoys have dispatched a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SENT into ENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act for someone else, as their representatives.

clue.text: Novice in order to turn up in blue mink?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the short word is read from the bottom

parts.note: OK means all correct, in order
L stands for learner, as on L-plates
the sky is blue

explanation.surface: A beginner arranging to display some blue fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' turns OK into KO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kolinsky is the Siberian mink, prized for its fur and for artists' brushes; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Christ's-thorn, for newly planted bank

indicators.note: replanting puts the letters of bank into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shrub has just been set into a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly planted' rearranges BANK.
explanation.definitionFit: The nabk is the thorny shrub held to have supplied the crown of thorns.

clue.text: What one gets down to is ABCs corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted letters have been scrambled from their proper order

explanation.surface: The essentials of learning are the alphabet garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges IS ABCS; the page drops the S that the letter count needs.
explanation.definitionFit: One 'gets down to basics' when attending to the fundamental matters first.

clue.text: Admitted is about to be among the old folk

indicators.note: among puts one piece inside another

parts.note: the aged are elderly people
RE is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Confessing one is about to join the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal; 'Admitted' reads as confessed, but here means conceded.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed, like admitted, means conceded or acknowledged as true.

clue.text: Oil is not to be blended with this type of alcohol

indicators.note: blending mixes the letters of oil is not together

explanation.surface: A recipe note saying the oil must not be mixed with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be blended' rearranges OIL IS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inositol is a sugar alcohol found in plant and animal tissue.

clue.text: Impaled upon reeds growing wild around the gardens

indicators.note: around puts one piece outside the other
plants growing wild are unruly, so the letters of reeds are jumbled

parts.note: Kew Gardens in London is the botanical garden

explanation.surface: Someone spiked on reeds running riot about the botanic gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' gives SERED, and 'around' is the container signal; Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered means pierced through with a spit or spike.

clue.text: Cover-up for disc jockey getting a label wrong

indicators.note: wrong letters are out of their right places, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A radio presenter's garment gets the wrong label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges A LABEL into ELLABA.
explanation.definitionFit: A djellaba is a long loose hooded robe worn in North Africa, a garment covering the whole body.

clue.text: Duck on Loire harassed another bird

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: harassed letters are pushed about into disorder

explanation.surface: A duck on a French river is bothered by another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harassed' rearranges LOIRE, the French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriole is a songbird, gold and black in many species; 'another' follows the duck.

clue.text: Toe Eric fractured should be set

indicators.note: a fractured thing is broken up, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Eric's broken toe needs setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fractured' rearranges TOE ERIC; 'set' looks like the medical verb but is a noun meaning a clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people, a set.

clue.text: Recording getting away from first group

parts.note: being away from somewhere means not in it

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word group

explanation.surface: Escaping from the leading band during a recording session.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means writing down or recording something.

clue.text: Rock, in old mourning ritual

parts.note: dole is an archaic word for grief or lamentation
a rite is a ritual

explanation.surface: A stone figures in an ancient funeral ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLE in the sense of sorrow is old-fashioned, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolerite is a dark, coarse igneous stone similar to basalt.

clue.text: Pole and Russian fought

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship
RED was the old term for a Soviet communist

explanation.surface: A man from Poland and one from Russia came to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a wooden spar.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue, so sparred means fought.

clue.text: Fish with the captain

definitions.meaning: a name for the saury, a long-beaked fish
the master of a boat or leader of a team

explanation.definitionFit: Both a long-snouted sea creature and the commander of a vessel or side bear this name.

clue.text: Chap will hold on, and is keener!

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside

parts.note: HE stands for a male, a chap

explanation.surface: A fellow clinging on, all the more eager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will hold' is the container signal; 'keener' is not more eager but a sharpener.
explanation.definitionFit: A hone is a whetstone that gives a blade a keen edge, so it is a keener.

clue.text: Authority for globe-trotters to proceed to the left?

parts.note: to pass is to go on, proceed
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Travellers are told to move along to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document that permits travel abroad.

clue.text: Keeper shot red iguana, out East

indicators.note: out means the letter is dropped
shot here means ruined, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper bags a lizard out east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges RED IGUANA, and 'out' then drops E for East.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian is a protector or custodian, someone who keeps watch.

clue.text: Horsemen? Yes, both

parts.note: not riders but creatures that are horse and man at once, both halves together

explanation.definitionFit: Centaurs in Greek myth have a man's upper body on a horse's body.

clue.text: Sky god has second opening in the body

parts.note: Anu was the Mesopotamian god of the sky

explanation.surface: An ancient deity owns another orifice.
explanation.definitionFit: The anus is the excretory orifice at the end of the gut.

clue.text: Aintree spill for the apprentice

indicators.note: a spill throws things into disorder, so the letters of Aintree are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tumble at the Liverpool racecourse for the novice jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spill' rearranges AINTREE, the racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a trade, like an apprentice.

clue.text: Set out with first mate to stow the cargo

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are disordered

parts.note: Eve was the first wife, Adam's mate

explanation.surface: Departing with the chief officer to load the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into STE; 'first mate' is not a ship's officer but Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To steeve is a nautical verb meaning to pack cargo tightly in a hold.

clue.text: University girl struggles over first exam-and it gets even nastier

indicators.note: struggling letters writhe into a new order
first picks the opening letter of exam

explanation.surface: A student battles through her first test, which only gets worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' rearranges GIRL with E (exam's first letter) into GLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglier means more unpleasant or more hostile.

clue.text: Mole providing false gen, taking in trendy Australian chap

indicators.note: taking in puts one piece inside another
false information is distorted, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: in Australian slang a roy is a fashionable young man

explanation.surface: A spy feeds bad intelligence to a hip Aussie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' gives GNE, and 'taking in' is the container signal; gen is informal British for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a breakwater or sea wall, like a groyne built against erosion.

clue.text: They guarantee certain fixtures, apparently

parts.note: sure means certain
ties are matches in a sporting fixture list

explanation.surface: Bookmakers' sure bets on sports matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' signals the playful split of the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sureties are guarantors who take on liability for another's debts or conduct.

clue.text: The old one familiar with the boards

definitions.text: The old one familiar with the boards

parts.words: The old one familiar with the boards
parts.note: an experienced hand, playfully taken as an actor who knows the stage, 'the boards'

explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran; literally the word suggests a person of the theatre.

clue.text: Spirits raised by Scotch mist

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the word is read upwards

parts.note: rums are spirits

explanation.surface: Whisky drinkers lifted by Highland drizzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses RUMS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Smur is a Scots word for fine drizzle.

clue.text: Duck exists on fruit

parts.note: a cricket duck is a zero score, O
lives means exists

explanation.surface: A duck that survives on berries.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are small stone fruits of the olive tree.

clue.text: Freedom to claim I am a weakling without sex-appeal

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: without means outside here, round the other piece

parts.note: a puny person is a weakling
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man claims exemption because he is feeble and unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, the container signal; IT for sex appeal is dated slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is exemption from punishment, freedom from consequences.

clue.text: Proposal requires careful handling

definitions.meaning: a formal offer or bid for a contract
sore or delicate, needing gentle treatment

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a bid and an adjective for something sensitive.

clue.text: Save by making your own jam?

definitions.meaning: to keep from harm or decay
playfully, a homemade jam is a ... you make yourself

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to keep safe and is also a noun for jam or bottled fruit.
